output.reason: Evidence supports that (i) for non-individual (corporate) borrowers, a 2% foreclosure charge applies (and this can be consistent with a pre-payment/foreclosure fee), and (ii) for loans/advances sanctioned or renewed on/after Jan 1, 2026, a UCB must clearly disclose the applicability of pre-payment charges in the sanction letter and loan agreement, and must not charge any pre-payment charges that were not disclosed. However, the claim is not fully supported because it (a) treats the 2% foreclosure charge as a “pre-payment charge” without explicit linkage in the evidence, and (b) omits the evidence’s specific scope/condition that these disclosure/no-undisclosed-charging rules apply only to loans/advances sanctioned or renewed on or after January 1, 2026. The “does not conflict … on its face” conclusion is therefore only partly grounded.
